identity.name: Azure Conditional-Access & Mailbox-Rule Persistence (SIM-ITDR-019)
identity.summary: An identity actor weakens the Entra ID conditional-access posture (adds/updates/deletes a CA policy) then plants a covert inbox-rule that auto-forwards mail externally. azure_audit_emitter streams the CA-policy record (msft_azure_audit) and m365_activity_emitter the Exchange New-InboxRule (msft_o365_audit), so XSIAM Analytics alerts and ABIOCs fire on the two-stage persistence chain.
identity.description: Validates the XSIAM 'Azure Audit Log' data-source Analytics alerts 'Azure conditional access policy creation or modification' and 'Azure mailbox rule creation'. The technique models a common cloud-identity persistence chain (T1556 Modify Authentication Process → T1114.003 Email Forwarding Rule): an attacker who has obtained a privileged/service-principal identity relaxes the conditional-access enforcement that would otherwise block their session, then establishes covert collection via an external auto-forwarding inbox rule. The card ships the two Analytics alerts as rule-based XQL bodies plus two auto-tuned ABIOCs (deviation from the learned per-admin CA-change / per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline) and a correlation rule that stitches the CA weakening (msft_azure_audit) and the mail-rule creation (msft_o365_audit) into a single Azure identity-persistence incident on temporal co-occurrence within the persistence window.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-019 — azure_audit_emitter (event_pattern conditional_access_policy_change) drives the Azure Activity Log CA-policy leg into msft_azure_audit; m365_activity_emitter (event_pattern mailbox_rule_creation) drives the Exchange New-InboxRule leg into msft_o365_audit.

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP log collector is wired into Cortex XSIAM as the Azure Audit Log / Microsoft 365 third-party source so the emitted records land in msft_azure_audit and msft_o365_audit.

payload.code:
# Emit the two-stage Azure identity-persistence chain via the analytics streamer.
# Leg 1: conditional-access policy modification -> msft_azure_audit
# Leg 2: external auto-forwarding inbox rule creation -> msft_o365_audit
set -euo pipefail
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/itdr-019.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP collector wired into XSIAM as the Azure Audit Log / M365 source.

input_variables.name: TARGET_USER
input_variables.description: Initiating identity whose Azure Audit Log / mailbox the synthetic persistence records are attributed to.

expected_artifacts.description: Azure Activity Log record (msft_azure_audit) for a conditional-access policy write operation attributed to the initiating app identity (identity.claims.appid).
O365 audit record for a New-InboxRule / Set-InboxRule with an external ForwardTo/RedirectTo target.

abiocs.name: Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline
abiocs.description: Auto-tuned ABIOC — an identity or service principal whose learned baseline is a low, stable cadence of conditional-access changes suddenly updates or deletes CA policies (relaxing MFA / device-compliance / location enforcement). Fires on the deviation from the per-actor CA-change baseline, anchored to the identity causality chain rather than any single known-bad operation.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter operationName = "MICROSOFT.AADIAM/CONDITIONALACCESS/POLICIES/WRITE" and category = "Administrative"
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| alter actor_app = identity -> claims -> appid, actor_oid = identity -> claims -> objectidentifier
| comp count() as ca_changes_now, earliest(_time) as first_change by actor_app, actor_oid
| join type=left (dataset = msft_azure_audit | filter operationName = "MICROSOFT.AADIAM/CONDITIONALACCESS/POLICIES/WRITE" and category = "Administrative" | filter _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600) | alter actor_app = identity -> claims -> appid | comp count() as learned_ca_change_cadence by actor_app) as baseline baseline.actor_app = actor_app
| alter learned_ca_change_cadence = coalesce(learned_ca_change_cadence, 0)
| filter ca_changes_now >= 1 and learned_ca_change_cadence = 0
| fields actor_app, actor_oid, ca_changes_now, learned_ca_change_cadence, first_change
abiocs.causality_anchor: The learned per-application/service-principal conditional-access change baseline (which app identities normally issue MICROSOFT.AADIAM/CONDITIONALACCESS/POLICIES/WRITE, at what cadence); the ABIOC anchors its deviation to the initiating app identity (identity.claims.appid) in the Azure Activity Log audit chain.

abiocs.name: External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline
abiocs.description: Auto-tuned ABIOC — a mailbox that has never (or rarely) created client-side inbox rules suddenly creates a New-InboxRule/Set-InboxRule (the external ForwardTo target is carried in the rule's Parameters array). Fires on the first-seen deviation from the per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline, part of the same persistence campaign as the preceding conditional-access weakening.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| alter mailbox = UserId, rule_name = RuleName
| comp count() as inbox_rules_now, earliest(_time) as first_rule by mailbox, rule_name
| join type=left (dataset = msft_o365_audit | filter Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule") | filter _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600) | alter mailbox = UserId | comp count() as learned_inbox_rule_cadence by mailbox) as baseline baseline.mailbox = mailbox
| alter learned_inbox_rule_cadence = coalesce(learned_inbox_rule_cadence, 0)
| filter inbox_rules_now >= 1 and learned_inbox_rule_cadence = 0
| fields mailbox, rule_name, inbox_rules_now, learned_inbox_rule_cadence, first_rule
abiocs.causality_anchor: The learned per-mailbox inbox-rule baseline (whether this mailbox normally creates client-side inbox rules); fires on the first-seen rule creation for a mailbox with no prior rule-creation history, correlated to the preceding conditional-access change within the persistence campaign window.

xql_queries.name: Azure conditional access policy creation or modification
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter operationName = "MICROSOFT.AADIAM/CONDITIONALACCESS/POLICIES/WRITE" and category = "Administrative"
| alter actor_app = identity -> claims -> appid, actor_oid = identity -> claims -> objectidentifier, caller_ip = callerIpAddress
| comp count() as change_count, values(operationName) as operations by actor_app, actor_oid, caller_ip
| filter change_count >= 1
| fields actor_app, actor_oid, caller_ip, operations, change_count

xql_queries.name: Azure mailbox rule creation
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| alter mailbox = UserId, rule_name = RuleName, rule_object = ObjectId
| comp count() as rule_events, values(Operation) as operations by mailbox, rule_name, rule_object
| filter rule_events >= 1
| fields mailbox, rule_name, rule_object, operations, rule_events

xql_queries.name: Azure Audit Log persistence signals landed in datasets
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_audit
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900) and operationName = "MICROSOFT.AADIAM/CONDITIONALACCESS/POLICIES/WRITE"
| alter signal = "ca_policy_change"
| fields signal, _time
| union (dataset = msft_o365_audit | filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900) and Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule") | alter signal = "inbox_rule_create" | fields signal, _time)
| comp count() as observed_events by signal
| filter observed_events >= 1
| fields signal, observed_events

correlation_rules.name: Azure Identity Persistence — CA policy weakening then covert mail rule
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when analytics `Azure conditional access policy creation or modification` (or abioc `Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline`) on msft_azure_audit and analytics `Azure mailbox rule creation` (or abioc `External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline`) on msft_o365_audit both fire within a 30-minute persistence window. The two legs land in different datasets with different identity fields (the CA record carries identity.claims.appid; the inbox-rule record carries UserId), so the rule stitches on temporal co-occurrence within the campaign window rather than a single shared identity-field value, raising one two-stage Azure identity-persistence incident: the actor first relaxes conditional-access enforcement, then plants a covert external mail-forwarding rule for collection.

threat_scenarios.name: Azure identity persistence — conditional-access weakening and covert mailbox forwarding
threat_scenarios.description: POV use case proving the Azure Audit Log Analytics alerts and their auto-tuned ABIOCs fire on a two-stage Entra ID / M365 persistence chain, and that XSIAM correlation stitches both legs into a single incident on temporal co-occurrence within the persistence window.

threat_steps.objective: The 'Azure conditional access policy creation or modification' Analytics alert (and the CA-weakening ABIOC) fire when a CA policy is updated/deleted off the learned admin-change baseline.
preconditions: The Azure Audit Log source is ingesting into msft_azure_audit.
Cortex has learned a per-identity conditional-access change baseline.
steps: Run azure_audit_emitter to stream a conditional-access policy update/delete record.
Observe the Analytics alert and the CA-weakening ABIOC fire on the initiating identity.
success_criteria: Analytics `Azure conditional access policy creation or modification` fires within the MTTD budget.
ABIOC `Conditional-access policy weakened off the learned admin-change baseline` fires on the same actor.

threat_steps.objective: The 'Azure mailbox rule creation' Analytics alert (and the external-forwarding ABIOC) fire on an external auto-forwarding inbox rule, and correlation CR-ITDR-0019 stitches both legs into one incident.
preconditions: The Microsoft 365 audit source is ingesting into msft_o365_audit.
The conditional-access weakening from TC-ITDR-019A occurred within the correlation window (same persistence campaign).
steps: Run azure_audit_emitter to stream a New-InboxRule with an external ForwardTo target.
Observe the mailbox-rule Analytics alert and the external-forwarding ABIOC fire.
Confirm correlation CR-ITDR-0019 raises one stitched Azure identity-persistence incident.
success_criteria: Analytics `Azure mailbox rule creation` fires within the MTTD budget.
ABIOC `External mailbox forwarding rule off the learned inbox-rule baseline` fires on the same mailbox.
Correlation `CR-ITDR-0019` raises exactly one stitched incident.

preventive_controls: Protect conditional-access policy administration behind privileged-identity-management (PIM) just-in-time elevation and require approval for CA policy changes.
Block or alert on Exchange Online mailbox rules that forward or redirect to external recipients (transport-rule guardrail + external-forwarding disabled by default).
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all identities that can modify conditional-access policy.
detection_engineering: Baseline which identities and service principals normally modify conditional-access policy and at what cadence; alert on off-baseline CA update/delete operations.
Alert on any inbox rule creation whose ForwardTo/RedirectTo target is an external domain, especially when it closely follows a conditional-access change by the same identity.
Correlate the CA-weakening and mailbox-rule legs within a short persistence window to raise a single high-confidence persistence incident.
